description.narrative: Inline with the identified WASH need sand WASH cluster priorities, the proposed project aims to Reduce the sufferings of conflict affected women, men, boys and girls across the Gaza strip Governorates through provision of adequate water and sanitation services. The proposed response prioritizes delivery of timely water, sanitation and hygiene promotion activities to internally displaced people in IDP and Returnee sites post the ceasefire halt and in hard to reach areas across the governorates of the Gaza Strip. Building on the achievements of Phase I, this second phase of the WASH intervention aims to sustain and expand life-saving WASH services to vulnerable populations, particularly IDPs in Khan Younis, the Middle Area, and North Gaza. The implementation is rooted in Oxfam’s multi-sectoral emergency strategy and continues to align with WASH Cluster priorities, UNICEF technical guidance, and Sphere Standards. Implementation will be led by Oxfam with support from localized technical actors, ensuring a context-sensitive and community-based approach. Phase II targets key WASH outputs with expanded scope and geographic reach, addressing the protracted displacement crisis and the strain on fragile WASH infrastructure. Under Output 1.1, 80,000 individuals (13,333 HHs or units) will benefit from increased access to safe domestic water. Approximately 6.5 km of water networks and two water wells will be rehabilitated (4 km funded by UNICEF; 2.5 km and two wells through Oxfam co-financing). The intervention includes provision and installation of water pipes and fittings. Water quality surveillance will be strengthened through engagement of technical support to carry out routine testing 20 days/month over six months, allowing for continuous monitoring and corrective actions. For Output 1.2, 14,850 people (2,475 HHs), including PWDs and CWDs, will benefit from improved sanitation. A total of 1,800 shared emergency latrines will be installed with gender-segregated access at the household level. Latrine slabs will be sourced internationally or locally depending on access constraints. Desludging operations will be supported through a hybrid model using desludging trucks, 15 manual desludging kits, PPE, and labor assistance, including the use of animal-drawn transport where vehicle access is limited. Hand hygiene will be reinforced through installation of emergency hand washing stations and regular provision of liquid soap. Under Output 1.3, access to basic water services will be provided to 50,000 individuals (8,333 HHs) through water trucking and installation of water storage infrastructure. This includes30 bladders supplied by UNICEF and 50 community tanks (1m³ capacity) to be procured based on access feasibility. These efforts aim to maintain safe and reliable water access in informal IDP camps, shelters, and host communities. Under Output 1.4, 31,360 people (5,227 HHs) will receive emergency hygiene kits and essential WASH NFIs, with priority to vulnerable groups such as PWDs and CWDs. Hygiene promotion activities will reach 14,850 individuals through door-to-door awareness sessions, community-led initiatives, trainingof community mobilizers, and dissemination of context-adapted IEC materials. Mobilizers will receive structured support and incentives to ensure consistent outreach over three months. Under Output 1.5, 15 healthcare facilities; mainly governmental ones will receive WASH support to benefit 15,000 individuals. This will be coordinated with Health actors and with Health section as required. Activities include repair of water and sanitation systems, distribution of public health IEC materials, training of healthcare personnelon hygiene promotion and water related massages, and community outreach led by trained facilitators working within the facilities for two months. Output 1.6 provides a contingency mechanism to address emerging WASH priorities identified by UNICEF in coordination with the WASH Cluster. These resources will ensure flexible, rapid response to unforeseen needsor scale-up during the project’s lifetime, subject to UNICEF’s prior approval. The strategy continues to emphasize community participation, gender equity, and inclusive design. All interventions adhere to UNICEF WASH technical guidance, Sphere Standards, and relevant Gaza-specific protocols, including water trucking and sanitation guidelines and Hygiene Promotion TWiG resources. Procurement plans are structured to balance timeliness, cost-efficiency, and contingency for access restrictions. Building on the operational foundations and learning from Phase I, this intervention will reinforce resilience through a localized delivery model, adaptive management, and coordinated response mechanisms, ensuring essential WASH services reach the most affected populations with dignity and consistency

participating-org.narrative:
Oxfam Novib has been active in the Occupied Palestinian Territory/Israel (OPT/I) since 1982 and working with Palestinian refugees in Lebanon since the mid 1980s. It has built up a strong network of relationships with local NGOs and counts among its localcounterparts some of the largest and most professional NGOs in various sectors. It has accompanied these NGOs in their development from ad hoc volunteer groups to sizeable professional institutions with national outreach. At the same time the conceptualisation of the programme has evolved from three country programs in the early 1990s to a program for Palestinians in the Middle East (PME) working withPalestinians in OPT, Israel and Lebanon.
The programme has changed over the years with the establishment of the Palestinian Authority (PA) in the mid-1990s from a focus on support and service provision at a grassroots level and grassroots mobilization, to working towards influencing the establishment of the PA, its lawmaking and supporting building a democratic state # this involved supporting efforts of Palestinian civil society to build the basis for a democratic Palestinian state with room for civil participation, ensuring inclusion of vulnerable groups, refugees and women, and shaping its laws and systems. Oxfam Novib has also supported partners that are working on the provision of humanitarian assistance, response preparedness and conflict transformation. We have also supported partners in the provision of health services, access to quality education and gender justice.
